If your train is waitlisted, ask for a confirmed departure from a second rail terminal and a truck quote to the same delivery address. For repeat container loads to Kazakhstan or Uzbekistan, rail can still be a sensible starting point. For a deadline shipment to Kyrgyzstan or Tajikistan, an executable road booking may be easier to plan around. For Turkmenistan, check transit approvals and the final delivery leg before comparing prices. On Europe-bound cargo, ask which borders and ferry legs are included. November booking reports show why this matters. One train can be sold out while another serving the same region still has space.

  • Compare the first credible pickup and delivery dates for each option.
  • Ask for a train allocation or a confirmed truck dispatch window in writing.
  • Price each option to the same address, with border handling and onward delivery shown.

What changed in November

The conflict around the Gulf continues to affect both carrier acceptance and the cost of some services. Maersk's November 18 update lists destination and cargo restrictions. CMA CGM announced an emergency fuel surcharge effective November 1 for specified trades. If your original route uses Bandar Abbas, ask for a fresh China-to-Bandar Abbas offer with the same origin, equipment and service scope as the previous quote. Check the base rate, carrier acceptance, surcharge items and any onward or alternative port charges. Gulf carrier notices describe regional conditions. A comparable pair of quotes is what lets you measure the increase on your Iran shipment.

Rail pressure varies by departure. Zencargo's November 17 market update reported tight space at Jinhua and a sold-out Chengdu–Tilburg service for November, while it reported space from Chengdu to Łódź and at hubs including Xi’an, Chongqing and Wuhan. That snapshot shows several different conditions within the same network. The November ERAI report also described price decreases in its October Chengdu and Chongqing rail samples. A higher quote on a particular departure can therefore coexist with softer prices elsewhere. For a shipment booked today, get the train, cutoff and allocation in writing. If a quote is higher, request a line-by-line comparison with the previous quote to see whether the rail leg, equipment, origin pickup or final delivery changed.

Road and rail across the five Central Asian destinations

The table gives starting points for a quote. For every option, name the actual city and receiver. A quote to a rail terminal can leave a separate transfer and truck delivery to arrange.

DestinationWhat to compareWhat to confirm in the quotation
KazakhstanRail via Alashankou–Dostyk or Khorgos–Altynkol, or road via a named crossing such as Khorgos–Nur ZholyRail terminal, pickup status, delivery truck and charges at the receiving address
UzbekistanRail through Kazakhstan or road via Kazakhstan or KyrgyzstanIf using the Kyrgyz route, ask for the road crossing and vehicle handovers. Check final delivery to Tashkent or the specified city.
KyrgyzstanRoad for an address in Bishkek or Osh, with rail plus truck worth pricing if the terminal path suits the deliveryNamed border, vehicle handovers and confirmation of the onward truck. The China–Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan railway remains under construction.
TajikistanRoad via Karasu–Kulma, or an operator-quoted rail and road option into DushanbeBorder operating window and weather contingency on the road route. For intermodal, ask where the cargo changes mode and whether the departure can be booked.
TurkmenistanRoad via Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, or a rail option through the regional networkTransit permits and customs arrangements, destination terminal, border handover and Ashgabat delivery scope

IRU has documented routes to Tashkent through Kyrgyzstan and to Ashgabat through Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. Chinese embassy reporting also documents a Dushanbe intermodal pilot via Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan. Use those records to ask operators about current departures and cargo acceptance for your shipment.

When trucking can rescue a Europe delivery

Suppose you have an order for the Netherlands and your preferred train is full. Ask whether a different confirmed train into Poland, with a booked onward truck, still meets the warehouse appointment. In parallel, ask for an overland offer for the most urgent portion. A LinkedIn operator case described trucking to Aktau, a Caspian crossing to Baku, then a mix of road and rail toward Germany. The case gives a practical question to ask a forwarder. Which legs have booked capacity, and who is responsible when cargo misses a connection?

If the quote names the Middle Corridor, request the Caspian ports, ferry or vessel arrangement, transfers and onward EU delivery. If it uses a northern route, request all transit countries, the exact operators and written acceptance for your commodity. Have the broker and insurer review the route and cargo before committing. Ask whether the load stays sealed, changes trailers or is unloaded and reloaded. An offer described as road freight can still include a ferry or rail segment. That distinction affects arrival planning and who handles the shipment at each handoff.

Make the switch using a cutoff and an all-in quote

Give both providers the cargo-ready date, deadline, origin address, destination postcode, package count, dimensions, gross weight and product description. Ask for the cutoff for documents and physical loading, the first confirmed departure, estimated delivery range and the expiry of the rate. A groupage truck also needs a consolidation departure. On a dedicated truck, confirm when the vehicle will arrive and when it can cross.

Line up pickup, cross-border transfer, transit paperwork, waiting charges, any ferry, destination handling and last-mile delivery. Ask which items are included or charged when incurred. Set a decision time before rail cutoff or cancellation charges apply. If no rail allocation arrives by then, activate the quoted truck option for the time-critical portion. Where cargo can be split, a later confirmed train may still suit the balance. Send your shipment details for a route comparison.

Frequently asked questions

Is China–Europe rail fully booked?

Availability is specific to the departure and service. A sold-out route may have alternatives from another hub or to a nearby terminal. Ask for a confirmed booking with an onward delivery plan.

Does TIR guarantee a nonstop truck or a fixed delivery date?

TIR provides a framework for customs transit under guarantee. The dispatch window, vehicle handovers, inspections and delivery schedule still depend on the route and booking.

How can I tell whether the Iran sea rate has risen for my shipment?

Compare two dated offers for the same origin, destination, container type and service scope. Ask the forwarder to show which base rate or surcharge changed and whether the carrier still accepts the booking.
